newsitem.title: USA: USDA to hold meeting on meat, poultry SSOPs.
newsitem.headline: USDA to hold meeting on meat, poultry SSOPs.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Agriculture on Tuesday said it will hold a public meeting on written sanitation standard operating procedures (SSOPs) as the meat and poultry industry gears up to carry out the new procedures.
USDA said it will also discuss E. coli sampling requirements at the session, which is slated for January 23. Both requirements go into effect Jan. 27.
SSOPs is the first stage in the implementation of new meat inspection rules announced in July which are modelled on the food safety principle Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP).

Beginning Jan. 27, slaughter and processing plants must have SSOPs in place to prevent product contamination and ensure food safety and slaughter plants must begin testing for E. coli as a means of process control to prevent fecal contamination, USDA said.
USDA said it will operate a toll-free hotline from January 13 to February 14. The number is 1-800-256-7072.
